responsibility: This module implements GCC’s static analyzer, an interprocedural symbolic-execution subsystem built on GIMPLE and integrated as the -fanalyzer IPA pass. Its core files construct a supergraph over CFG and callgraph structure, represent analysis locations and calling context with program_point and call_string, and explore an exploded graph of program_state objects that combine a region-based symbolic memory model, symbolic values, stores, and constraint reasoning. Around that engine, the module provides interprocedural planning and call summaries, state purging and complexity controls to manage path explosion, and known-function modeling for builtins and common C/C++/POSIX APIs. It also hosts a generic state-machine framework and concrete checkers for resource lifetime and API misuse issues such as malloc/free, FILE streams, file descriptors, varargs, taint, signal safety, and sensitive-data flow, along with dedicated analyses for bounds errors, infinite loops, and infinite recursion. A substantial diagnostics layer then turns saved warnings into feasible, pruned checker paths with specialized events, text-art and XML state visualizations, and user-facing option handling, logging, dumps, and selftests, distinguishing this module as GCC’s path-sensitive bug-finding and diagnostic explanation subsystem rather than a language frontend or optimization pass.
